stem: In the Business Disability Forum's Accessibility Maturity Model, what characterizes Level 1?

options.text: Accessibility work is ad hoc and undocumented, without a formal process or policy.
options.rationale: Level 1 (Informal) is defined by the absence of documentation or process; accessibility work is ad hoc and undocumented.

options.text: Accessibility processes are monitored and improved as standard business practice across the organization.
options.shortLabel: Monitored and improved as business practice
options.rationale: Monitoring and improving processes as standard business practice defines Level 4 (Managed).

options.text: Accessibility policies and standards are documented, but they are not consistently actioned.
options.rationale: Documents exist but are not consistently actioned is the defining characteristic of Level 2 (Defined).

options.text: Accessibility practices and training are built into regular development, procurement, and content workflows.
options.rationale: Embedding consistent, repeatable processes, training, and tools across regular business operations characterizes Level 3 (Repeatable).

explanation: The Business Disability Forum's Accessibility Maturity Model benchmarks an organization's maturity across five levels: Level 1 (Informal - ad hoc, with no documentation or process in place), Level 2 (Defined - policies and standards are documented but not consistently actioned), Level 3 (Repeatable - processes are established and actioned consistently), Level 4 (Managed - processes are monitored and improved as standard business practice), and Level 5 (Best practice - continuous improvement and sharing of best practice).
